title: Matplotlib Plotting: X and Y Data
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Plotting: X and Y Data.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: The plot function maps x-values and y-values to a line or marker series. Both arrays should have compatible lengths. If x-values are omitted, Matplotlib uses sequential positions. Multiple calls add multiple series to the same Axes.
understand.whyItMatters: Correctly pairing x and y values is essential for accurate charts and meaningful comparisons.
understand.analogy: Each x-coordinate pairs with one y-coordinate to place a point on a map.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Plotting: X and Y Data is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Plot paired x and y values
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6])
print(line.get_ydata().tolist())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Each y value pairs with the x value at the same position.

examples.title: Use default x positions
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([7, 8, 9])
print(line.get_xdata().tolist())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: When x is omitted, positions start at zero.

examples.title: Draw multiple series
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2], [2, 4])
ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 6])
print(len(ax.lines))
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Each plot call adds another line.

examples.title: Attach a series label
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [2, 3], label='Forecast')
print(line.get_label())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Labels can later be displayed in a legend.

examples.title: Use a step draw style
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line, = ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 5], drawstyle='steps-post')
print(line.get_drawstyle())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Step draw styles emphasize discrete changes.
